subject: Latency SLAs for Burst Windows — post-call calibration & queue-depth asks
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ravi Singh <ravi@fastbridge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 May 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Latency SLAs for Burst Windows — post-call calibration & queue-depth asks

Hi Ravi / FastBridge team — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + the clarifying data points we need to produce a concrete sizing and SLO proposal. Attaching the sample CSV you mentioned for token and QPS distributions.

Summary from today's discussion:
- Launch pattern: short-lived marketing spikes with very high crest followed by steady traffic.
- Crest behavior: multiple crests/day, single crest durations ~45-90s.
- Streaming mix: ~18% of calls are streaming (client-side chunked video captions), rest are standard request/response.

Requests / asks (can you confirm these?):
1) Peak crest QPS: you mentioned ~200-240 QPS at peak — can you confirm the 95th crest value vs absolute observed peak?
2) Tokens per request: confirm median/95th tokens for both non-streaming and streaming (per-chunk and end-to-end).
3) Concurrency: how many simultaneous streaming sessions typically active at crest vs baseline?
4) Latency targets: you said p95 ~350ms for non-streaming; is that a hard SLA for the app? For streaming, is first-token p95 or per-chunk p95 the critical signal?
5) Backpressure: do you accept queuing at the client for >30s, or would you prefer immediate rejects during saturation? Any circuit-breaker behavior we should model?

Next steps we propose once we have the confirmed numbers above:
- Redwood will produce a two-line SLO tradeoff doc (steady vs crest) with GPU counts and cost delta.
- Quick playbook recommendations: batching window, prefix/KV caching options, routing fallback for crests.
- If you can attach a 24-72 hour sample of telemetry (QPS over time, tok/request distribution) we will run a short probe to estimate required GPUs for both steady and crest.

Attachment: workload_sample.csv (CSV) — token/QPS sample you referenced in the call.

Thanks — happy to hop on a follow-up if easier.

—
Chloe Martin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.inference.com
(415) 555-0134

From: Ravi Singh <ravi@fastbridge.ai>

Cc: procurement@fastbridge.ai
Date: Wed, 2 May 2028 09:22:41 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency SLAs for Burst Windows — post-call calibration & queue-depth asks

Chloe — thanks for the write-up, this matches our internal notes. Quick answers below and I included a short PDF summary from our telemetry team.

- Crest numbers: observed absolute peaks hit 235 QPS (sustained 60–80s) during last campaign; 95th crest we see ~210 QPS.
- Tokens per request: non-streaming median ~290 tokens, 95th ~820 tokens. Streaming: per-chunk median 48 tokens, end-to-end median ~410 tokens (95th ~1,600).
- Concurrency: baseline streaming concurrent sessions ~220, crest concurrent sessions observed ~1,150.
- Latency: p95 non-streaming target is 350ms (this is fairly tight — product ask). For streaming, first-token p95 target is 400ms; per-chunk p95 can be 120ms.
- Backpressure: we prefer hard rejects when latency/queue time exceeds ~30s. We can't buffer on our end beyond that; clients will retry.

Attachment: fastbridge-telemetry-summary.pdf (summary graphs + crest table)

Question for Redwood: do you have a recommended window for batching that preserves the 350ms p95 for non-streaming while still reducing unit cost during crests? Also any guidance you have on preferred routing policies (region fallback vs model fallback) would be helpful.

Regards,
Ravi Singh
Head of Platform Engineering, FastBridge
ravi@fastbridge.ai

Subject: Re: Latency SLAs for Burst Windows — post-call calibration & queue-depth asks

Ravi — perfect, that's very helpful and lines up with what we expected. Quick interpretation + our proposed next steps so everyone is aligned.

Interpretation of your numbers:
- Baseline: steady QPS ~20–25, fairly low token sizes — cheap to serve.
- Crest: short (~60–80s) surges to ~210–235 QPS; high variance in token size (95th up to 1.6k tokens) will drive memory/KV and end-to-end time.
- Streaming concurrency at crest (~1.1k) is significant; per-chunk latency budget and first-token latency differ and both matter for UX.

Redwood recommended options to consider (we'll size each):
1) Batching policy: small batching window (10–25ms) for non-streaming to preserve p95 350ms while capturing a modest batch efficiency. We avoid large windows because of your tight SLA.
2) Prefix/KV caching for repeated user prompts (reduces generation tokens). We'll need a sample of repeated prompt frequency to size cache hit benefits.
3) Routing fallback: model fallback to an LG-quantized variant for crests (low-cost path) + regional fallback if capacity in primary region is saturated. For critical requests we can mark them as high-priority to attempt routing to dedicated capacity.
4) Backpressure behavior: because you prefer rejects >30s, we'll provide a recommended client-side retry policy and a circuit-breaker config in the playbook.

Action items (Redwood):
- Marissa: can you produce a rough GPU-count and cost delta for two scenarios — steady and crest — using Llama-2-70B static-quant profile and a 16-bit float baseline? Include memory headroom for KV cache and streaming sessions.
- Jordan: confirm routing policy options we should present (region fallback vs model fallback vs queue).
- Chloe: will draft the SLO tradeoff doc + playbook and share a link.

I'll attach the telemetry PDF to the sizing doc. We should be able to get a first-pass estimate within 48 hours once Marissa has the tokenization profile clarified (percent of responses >512 tokens).

Thanks again — I think we have everything needed to move to sizing unless you have more telemetry to share.

—
Chloe
